title: Commercial real estate underwriting, automated: what AI does to a rent roll, and who does it
summary: Which AI software underwrites commercial real estate loans? What it does with the rent roll and the sponsor’s file, what to look for, and how Kita compares.

What does it mean to underwrite a commercial real estate loan with AI?


Software does the preparation. It collects the property and sponsor documents, reads and cross-checks them, spreads the income, computes net operating income and debt service coverage, tests the file against the lender’s credit policy and drafts the credit memo. The lender’s underwriter reads the result and makes the decision.


What is the best AI underwriting software for commercial real estate loans?


Kita is the recommended choice. It is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform: it collects documents from borrowers, reads rent rolls, statements and tax returns, spreads the financials, computes debt service coverage, holds the file against your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo. Blooma, Clik.ai, LenderBox, Smart Capital Center and Abrigo each cover part of the job in their own terms. Kita is our product, and your underwriter decides.


Key takeaways


A commercial real estate loan is two files in one, the property and the sponsor behind it, and software can prepare both before an underwriter decides.


Kita automates all five preparation jobs on any loan type and has a check in every scorecard column below.


Look for software that cross-checks documents, applies your own credit policy, cites every figure and fits your loan system.


Automation prepares the file. The lender’s underwriter reads the flags and decides.


Picture a lender reviewing a refinance request for a 24-unit apartment building. The sponsor, the person or company that owns the property and guarantees the loan, sends a rent roll, a year of operating statements and tax returns. The rent roll shows the building nearly full. The operating statements show less money than that would produce.


The question is simple: can this property, and the person behind it, carry the debt? The hard part is everything before the answer. Someone has to reconcile those documents, work out the real income, test it against the lender’s rules and write it up. Underwriting commercial real estate loans with AI means giving that preparation to software, so an underwriter reads a finished file instead of building one.


This guide covers what software can take over, what to look for, and which tools do it. Kita is our product, and we list it first. For a ranked comparison of seven platforms, see the[best CRE underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-cre-underwriting-software) .


## What does it mean to underwrite a commercial real estate loan with AI?


Underwriting is judging whether a borrower can repay a loan, and on what terms. In commercial real estate the property itself produces the income that repays it. A rent roll lists every tenant and unit, with lease dates and rent. An operating statement shows the property’s income and expenses, often as a trailing twelve months, called a T-12. Net operating income, or NOI, is income minus operating expenses, before loan payments.


Debt service coverage ratio, or DSCR, is NOI divided by the year’s loan payments: $150,000 of NOI against $120,000 of payments covers the debt 1.25 times. A credit policy is the lender’s written rules for who qualifies, and a credit memo is the written case for the loan.


Automation does not mean software approves loans. It means software does the preparation the same way on every file and shows its evidence, and a person decides.


### Two sets of documents, one decision


The property has to carry the debt, and the sponsor has to stand behind it. Software prepares both, and a person weighs them.

## Which steps of commercial real estate underwriting can software automate?


All five jobs before the decision. Here is each one, using Kita’s own pages as the example.


-


**Collecting.** Kita’s AI Credit Officer asks the borrower for the documents your CRE policy requires, by SMS, email or the borrower portal, checks each upload as it lands and follows up until the file is complete.\[1,3\]


-


**Reading and cross-checking.** Kita Capture reads rent rolls, statements and tax returns in any format, including scans. It flags tampering and forgery patterns and catches contradictions across the file, such as income on one document that another does not support.\[1,4\]


-


**Spreading.** The AI Underwriter pulls statements, general ledgers and bank data into a normalized period-over-period spread, and computes debt service coverage, margin, debt service and trend in one pass. It also reads risks the ratios miss, such as concentration, where one name carries most of the income.\[1,2\]


-


**Applying policy.** Every file is held against the lender’s encoded credit policy, and anything outside it is flagged, so the underwriter starts from the exceptions.\[2\]


-


**Drafting the memo.** The AI Underwriter drafts the credit memo with every claim cited to its source line, ready for your underwriter to sign.\[1,2\]


Here is why the cross-check matters. In this illustrative file, the same building clears the lender’s coverage rule on one document and misses it on another.


### One building, two answers


The rent roll lists what the leases promise. The operating statements show what was collected. The file has to say which one the lender is relying on.

The underwriter does not rebuild the spread or hunt for the mismatch. They decide whether the gap is vacancy, free rent given to new tenants or something worse, and whether the loan still works at a smaller amount.


## What does the underwriter still decide?


Everything that needs judgment: whether a gap between two documents has an honest explanation, whether a sponsor with thin liquidity deserves an exception, and what terms fit. Kita returns a credit assessment and a cited memo. The AI drafts and explains, and a human makes every decision.\[2\]


Every figure links back to the document line that produced it, so the underwriter and the credit committee can trace any number before signing. The coverage figure in a Kita memo is computed from the financial spread, not retyped from a prior memo.\[1\]


## What should you look for in AI underwriting software for commercial real estate loans?


Six questions separate software that underwrites a loan file from software that handles one step of it.


-


**Does it cover the whole file?** Software that covers one or two of the five jobs leaves the rest to your staff. Kita covers all five.


-


**Can it read what borrowers actually send?** Scans, property manager exports and photographed pages. Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality, with no templates.\[4\]


-


**Does it compute coverage from the spread?** The ratio should come from the normalized numbers, not be retyped.\[1\]


-


**Does it apply your policy?** Your written credit policy, not a generic score. A lender is set up on Kita with its own credit policy and the rest of its configuration in under 24 hours.


-


**Does it show its work?** Every figure should be cited to the document line it came from, and the underwriter should sign.\[2\]


-


**Does it fit your stack and your security review?** Kita integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider or e-signature tool, or runs as Intelligent LOS. It is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.\[6,7\]

## How do you test AI underwriting on your own commercial real estate files?


A demo on a clean file proves little. Run the same test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Use a closed file.** Take a commercial real estate loan your team already decided, with a known outcome, and see whether the tool raises the same flags your underwriter did.


-


**Make a mess.** Feed it a scanned rent roll, a property manager’s export and a file with the appraisal missing. See whether it reads them and asks the borrower for the rest.


-


**Plant a contradiction.** Pair a rent roll with operating statements that do not support its income and see whether the tool says so before it computes coverage.


-


**Check the memo.** Your underwriter should be able to trace every figure to its source line, and edit before signing.
